symbols.note: from gatekit symbols system --dll dx11 --full; no per-method address was found in bg3_dx11.exe for these methods (null); factory/constructor/update come from survey.csv, which prints them as bg3.exe+RVA, the same offsets the dx11 symbols users list shows
symbols.limits: reads/writes: the component views in the parameters of the system's exported methods. uses: the component operations (add, remove, get, has) its per-frame update performs through the engine's out-of-line helpers, itself or in a function it calls (depth 2), with the call site; kind index: a matched method reads the type's index and the operation is not known. Not listed: operations the compiler inlined, those deeper than depth 2, and what a method that is not the update does (e.g. a SystemLoad) - read its pseudo-code; an empty writes list is not "writes nothing".

does.text: Public entry that stores a (user entity, item entity, bool) in a use-request map. It is called from a server movement step (an unnamed function, EoCServer.dll+0xA69640) when the character that walked to a target may wield it according to the helper CanBeWieldedByCaster; the bool is whether GetTargetType returned value 2.
does.evidence: EoCServer.dll+0x364910 name; caller EoCServer.dll+0xA69640 read around the call (CanBeWieldedByCaster, GetTargetType, GetSystem). The meaning of the bool is a guess from the call.

does.text: Runs in this order: gather set-position requests, gather stop-use requests, ProcessStartUseRequests, ProcessSetPositionRequests, ProcessStopUseRequests, ProcessRemovedWielding, ProcessRemovedWielded, ProcessCancelOnLoadSavegame, ProcessedThrown, UpdateComponents, ProcessedEndReposeOnPickedUpEntity.

For each pending use request where both entities are alive, the user does not already have eoc::improvised_weapon::WieldingComponent, the item does not already have WieldedComponent, and no other user claims the same item this frame, it adds esv::improvised_weapon::PickUpRequestOneFrameComponent to the user entity, holding the item handle.
does.evidence: EoCServer.dll ProcessStartUseRequests read in parts: alive checks, has-component helpers FUN_18035ee00 and FUN_18035ecc0 resolved to WieldingComponent and WieldedComponent, add helper FUN_18035b390 resolved to PickUpRequestOneFrameComponent. The meaning of the first 'not' tests (that the checks were negative) was read from the nesting.

does.text: Turns requests into state. For a (user, item) pair where both are alive and neither is in the stop sets it adds eoc::improvised_weapon::WieldingComponent to the user, esv::improvised_weapon::PickUpDataComponent to the user and WieldedComponent to the item. For items that are wielded and lose their wielder it removes WieldedComponent and adds PreparingToBeReleasedEventOneFrameComponent and SetPositionOneFrameComponent; for users it removes WieldingComponent and PickUpDataComponent.
does.evidence: EoCServer.dll UpdateComponents read in parts: add helpers FUN_18035bd80, FUN_18035b1b0, FUN_18035bb80, FUN_18035b590, FUN_18035b780 resolved to those types; removals use type indexes of WieldedComponent, WieldingComponent, PickUpDataComponent. Which of the three input sets feeds which branch was not pinned down.

does.text: For a user with WieldingComponent whose item still has WieldedComponent, when a byte in the item's data and a value read from the user's data agree, adds esv::improvised_weapon::CancelRequestOneFrameComponent to the user. The meaning of that comparison is unknown.
does.evidence: EoCServer.dll ProcessStopUseRequests read around its one AddComponent; helper FUN_18035add0 resolved to CancelRequestOneFrameComponent.

does.text: For each entity of a set passed in, reads a list kept on it and adds esv::improvised_weapon::EndReposeRequestOneFrameComponent to every live handle in that list. What owns the list was not identified.
does.evidence: EoCServer.dll ProcessedEndReposeOnPickedUpEntity read: add helper FUN_18035afc0 resolved to EndReposeRequestOneFrameComponent; the list comes through FUN_18035cc50, not resolved.

does.text: By their query types: ProcessedThrown reads esv::thrown::EntityThrownRequestOneFrameComponent, ProcessCancelOnLoadSavegame the savegame-load component, ProcessSetPositionRequests ls::TransformComponent. These probably end a pick-up when the held item is thrown or a save is loaded and move a picked-up item, but this is a guess from names; none was read for what it changes (none contains an Add or Remove component call).
does.evidence: query types and absence of AddComponent/RemoveComponent in the pseudo-code of these methods; EoCServer.dll.
